title: Hearing Louis Armstrong through the wall of the Sunset Cafe
summary: Outside the Sunset Cafe he heard a trumpet, learned it was Louis Armstrong, and resolved to be a jazz musician.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I'm telling you; it was rough. And when you mean rough, it means rough. It -- I always figure, figure that my ..... someday my ship will come in. And I'm beginning to, at that time beginning to see the dawn comin' up by listening in front of the Sunset Cafe and hearing this trumpet blowing through the walls. It looks like the wall's gonna crumble. And I wasn't the only one in front of the Sunset. There was other people that came back -- they didn't have the money to go in -- just listening, just, just listen and see who was blowin'. About the second or a third night I was there, I finally got nerve enough to ask one of the listeners outside in the sidewalk. I said, 'Who was that blowing?' And a -- 'Oh you don't know? There, I'll show you.' He took me over in front of the place, and I saw the picture, and under the picture with the horn, the trumpet, under there was the

name, Louis Armstrong. Mind you, this wasn't really, this was way before he was called Sachmo, but as we know him now, he's Sachmo. But at that time, I heard, when I heard Louis, that was the most beautiful he, he -- I, I was more determined to be a jazz musician. I think I and, and many, many musicians have used Lou Armstrong as our base -- our, their main reason to be in jazz because of the way that -- oh, here I come with the projection again -- the way he was projected by singing, by his improvisations and by the rhythms. That's personality. There, there isn't anything out of, out of the ordinary to -- that, that, that won't describe Armstrong. He, he's a prince. He's, he's one of the greatest. I mean . . .
